raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Make `AsyncLLM.abort()` terminate streaming-input sessions that are still waiting for their first input chunk. The input task is cancelled and the output iterator finishes without yielding an output.

Addresses the explicit-abort case in [this comment on #57061](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57061#issuecomment-6310672263), rather than the original issue's cancellation-during-registration case.

## Claims

- An external or internal abort before the first chunk stops the input producer and wakes the output consumer, including when the producer task has not started.
- Repeated aborts do not prevent a subsequent request from using the same external request ID.
- Existing processing takes over after the first request is registered; model execution and sampling are unchanged.

## Validation

Validated on base `2fb320d8304381e224dd27fbf8c13c30b4e1020f`: Python 3.12, Torch 2.14.0+cu130, one RTX 4090, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, TP=1, eager execution. The editable install uses the preceding commit's official wheel (`85e199e60ca87a4b136aeaa0842541139b94c778`); CUDA/C++ sources, CMake configuration and CUDA requirements are unchanged between them.

For the red runs, the new tests were retained while only `async_llm.py` and `output_processor.py` were restored to the base commit. The fixed versions were then restored for the green runs.

| Check | Base + new tests | With fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Three CPU regressions | 3 failed | 3 passed within the 10-test frontend suite |
| Real-model first-chunk regression | 1 failed (`TimeoutError`) | 1 passed |
| All selected frontend CPU tests | — | 10 passed |
| Adjacent collector / streaming-input tests | — | 6 passed |
| Real-model tokens emitted after abort | 4 | 0 |
| Input generator closed before its first chunk was released | false | true |
| Subsequent normal request using the same ID | 4 tokens | 4 identical tokens |

Commands, using exactly one available GPU for the last test:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/test_async_llm_streaming.py -k 'not e2e' -q
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py -k 'collector or streaming_input' -q
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$GPU_UUID" .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/test_async_llm_streaming.py::test_abort_stream_before_first_chunk_e2e -q
```

The GPU test uses real weights and EngineCore through public `AsyncLLM.generate()` / `abort()`. CPU cases replace only the remote EngineCore service. Event barriers force the ordering. The existing `v1-executor-worker` CI step selects the tests and their source dependencies.

All 17 applicable configured pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed. Hooks were selected using pre-commit's file/type filters and `always_run`, then invoked individually. Installing the entire hook set was blocked by the unrelated actionlint Go download; no applicable hook was omitted.

Normal-request tokens were `[0, 358, 2776, 4460]` in both versions. No model-quality or throughput improvement is claimed.

## Details

Before the first chunk, `_add_streaming_input_request()` has returned a collector and started an input task, but there is no `RequestState` or external-to-internal request mapping yet. `abort_requests()` therefore finds nothing; a later chunk is submitted normally.

Pending collectors now remain discoverable by abort. Abort removes the entry, cancels the input task and sends `STREAM_FINISHED` directly, including when the task has not started and cannot run its `finally`. The first request registration or task completion removes the pending entry.

State and abort's scan are proportional to streams awaiting their first input. There is no GPU synchronization or per-token work; scheduler, KV-cache and model-runner behavior are unchanged.

Issue comments and open-PR searches found no duplicate of this pre-first-chunk explicit-abort fix. Related work has distinct scope:

- #57062: cancellation while `add_request()` is in progress.
- #58942: terminal handling and preventing later chunks from reviving a registered session.
- #62871: suppressing the final request after input-processing failure.
- #53321 / #59339: scheduler handling of already admitted streaming requests.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with diagnosis, implementation.

@@ -38,6 +38,16 @@ Engine classes for offline and online inference.
 - [vllm.LLMEngine][]
 - [vllm.AsyncLLMEngine][]
 
+### Cancelling streaming input
+
+When [AsyncLLM.generate][vllm.v1.engine.async_llm.AsyncLLM.generate] consumes an
+asynchronous generator of [StreamingInput][vllm.engine.protocol.StreamingInput],
+you can cancel the session with `await engine.abort(request_id)` even while it is
+waiting for its first input chunk. If aborted before that chunk, the input task is
+cancelled and the output iterator ends without yielding any output. No
+configuration change is required, and the same request ID can be reused for a
+subsequent request.
+
 ## Inference Parameters
 
 Inference parameters for vLLM APIs.

+        ),
+    )
+    service = MagicMock()
+    service.resources.engine_dead = False
+    service.get_supported_tasks_async = AsyncMock(return_value=("generate",))
+    outputs: asyncio.Queue[EngineCoreOutputs] = asyncio.Queue()
+
+    async def submit(request):
+        if request.resumable:
+            outputs.put_nowait(
+                EngineCoreOutputs(
+                    outputs=[
+                        EngineCoreOutput(
+                            request_id=request.request_id,
+                            new_token_ids=[7],
+                            finish_reason=FinishReason.LENGTH,
+                        )
+                    ]
+                )
+            )
+
+    service.get_output_async = AsyncMock(side_effect=outputs.get)
+    service.add_request_async = AsyncMock(side_effect=submit)
+    service.abort_requests_async = AsyncMock()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        EngineCoreClient, "make_async_mp_client", MagicMock(return_value=service)
+    )
+    engine = AsyncLLM(config, UniProcExecutor, log_stats=False, log_requests=False)
+    try:
+        yield engine
+    finally:
+        engine.shutdown()
+        if engine.output_handler is not None:
+            await asyncio.gather(engine.output_handler, return_exceptions=True)
+
+
+async def _abort_before_first_chunk(engine: AsyncLLM) -> list[int]:
+    """Explicit abort closes both sides of a stream awaiting its first input."""
+    entered, release, closed = asyncio.Event(), asyncio.Event(), asyncio.Event()
+    yielded = []
+
+    async def inputs():
+        entered.set()
+        try:
+            await release.wait()
+            yielded.append(True)
+            yield StreamingInput(prompt={"prompt_token_ids": [1, 2, 3]})
+        finally:
+            closed.set()
+
+    async def consume():
+        return [
+            output
+            async for output in engine.generate(
+                inputs(),
+                SamplingParams(max_tokens=4, output_kind=RequestOutputKind.DELTA),
+                "before-first",
+            )
+        ]
+
+    consumer = asyncio.create_task(consume())
+    try:
+        await asyncio.wait_for(entered.wait(), 5)
+        await engine.abort("before-first")
+        assert await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(consumer), 5) == []
+        await asyncio.wait_for(closed.wait(), 5)
+        assert not yielded
+        assert engine.get_num_unfinished_requests() == 0
+
+        # Repeated aborts must not poison a new session using the same ID.
+        await engine.abort("before-first")
+
+        async def healthy_inputs():
+            yield StreamingInput(prompt={"prompt_token_ids": [1, 2, 3]})
+
+        async def reuse_id():
+            return [
+                token
+                async for output in engine.generate(
+                    healthy_inputs(),
+                    SamplingParams(
+                        temperature=0,
+                        max_tokens=1,
+                        ignore_eos=True,
+                        output_kind=RequestOutputKind.DELTA,
+                    ),
+                    "before-first",
+                )
+                for completion in output.outputs
+                for token in completion.token_ids
+            ]
+
+        return await asyncio.wait_for(reuse_id(), 30)
+    finally:
+        consumer.cancel()
+        await asyncio.gather(consumer, return_exceptions=True)
+        release.set()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.cpu_test
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_abort_stream_before_first_chunk(streaming_frontend):
+    assert await _abort_before_first_chunk(streaming_frontend) == [7]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_abort_stream_before_first_chunk_e2e():
+    engine = AsyncLLM.from_engine_args(
+        AsyncEngineArgs(
+            model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
+            enforce_eager=True,
+            max_model_len=256,
+            max_num_batched_tokens=128,
+            max_num_seqs=2,
+            gpu_memory_utilization=0.2,
+            enable_prefix_caching=False,
+            disable_log_stats=True,
+        )
+    )
+    try:
+        assert len(await _abort_before_first_chunk(engine)) == 1
+    finally:
+        engine.shutdown()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.cpu_test
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("internal", [False, True])
+async def test_abort_stream_before_producer_starts(streaming_frontend, internal):
+    """Cancellation before task startup must also finish the output collector."""
+    engine = streaming_frontend
+    entered = asyncio.Event()
+
+    async def inputs():
+        entered.set()
+        yield StreamingInput(prompt={"prompt_token_ids": [1, 2, 3]})
+
+    collector = await engine.add_request(
+        "not-started",
+        inputs(),
+        SamplingParams(max_tokens=4, output_kind=RequestOutputKind.DELTA),
+    )
+    try:
+        await engine.abort(
+            collector.request_id if internal else "not-started", internal=internal
+        )
+        assert await asyncio.wait_for(collector.get(), 5) is STREAM_FINISHED
+        assert not entered.is_set()
+    finally:
+        collector.close()
+        await engine.abort("not-started")

         a parent request, in which case the associated child requests are aborted
